creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews guest Matt McCall of Monument Traders Alliance about investing through a wave of system shutdowns — grounded flights after an FAA disruption, bank outages — that have pushed the VIX to its highest level since March. McCall's core argument is that long-term investors should not make long-term decisions on short-term fear: a five-hour airspace closure does not change a company's earnings outlook, and capitulation moments are usually buying opportunities, since nothing can slow innovation in the long term. He pitches three stocks that benefit when systems fail. Eaton (ETN), a $131bn electrical-grid and backup-power supplier, is a core holding: earnings expected to grow 15–18% a year, forward P/E around 20, PEG just above 1, with grid modernisation a decade-long tailwind even without AI. A10 Networks (ATEN), a $2.3bn cybersecurity firm that blocks traffic-flood attacks and routes legitimate traffic, trades at about 25x forward earnings versus CrowdStrike at 147x, despite being up nearly 90% this year. Parsons (PSN), a $5.5bn critical-infrastructure firm, just won a nearly $600m FAA contract extension to modernise air traffic control; EPS is expected at $2.46 this year and $3.39 next, a forward P/E of about 15, with price-to-sales below 1 and 98% institutional ownership. Calls: ETN BUY, ATEN BUY, PSN BUY — no entry prices stated. Note: captions garble 'Eaton' as 'Eat/Eaten' and 'bear markets' as 'bare markets'.
